elements.element: Mutual cap expressed as the greater of two limbs
elements.evidence: "each Party's total aggregate liability ... shall not exceed the greater of (a) ... and (b) One Million Dollars ($1,000,000)"

elements.element: Fee limb = fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim
elements.evidence: "in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim" — anchored to the event, not the claim
"neither Party shall be liable to the other for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages"

elements.element: Uncapped carve-out for breach of confidentiality
elements.evidence: "Except for Excluded Claims ... breach of its confidentiality obligations under Section 8"

elements.element: Uncapped carve-out for data protection and security obligations
elements.evidence: "or of its data protection or security obligations"

elements.element: Uncapped carve-out for infringement of the other party's IP
elements.evidence: "its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights"

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes
elements.evidence: "The Company's obligations to pay amounts due under Sections 3 and 4.2 are not subject to this Section 10.9" — limited to two sections rather than all amounts due / not damages
"each Party's total aggregate liability ... shall not exceed the greater of (a) the amounts paid or payable by the Company to HDI ... in the twelve (12) months"
"breach of its confidentiality obligations under Section 8"

elements.element: Carve-out for gross negligence and wilful misconduct

reasons: The fee limb is anchored to "the event giving rise to the claim" rather than the claim itself; use "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" to hit the locked preferred wording.

The payment-obligations sentence is narrowed to "amounts due under Sections 3 and 4.2" and does not state that such obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes; broaden to all amounts due under the Agreement.

All preferred carve-outs (confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnity, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) and the mutual consequential-damages exclusion are present and uncapped.
The insertion is a concise new clause where none existed, changes nothing else, and introduces no undefined terms or dangling mechanics, so minimality and intent are preserved.
Net effect: the clause lands at the fallback (mutual 12 months' fees cap with required carve-outs) but misses two precision elements of the locked preferred target.
